rationale: This is a tiny Shootout-style benchmark (9 functions, 634 bytes of text) dominated by hot, tightly-looped drivers (ackermann, fib2, ary3, hash, heapsort, nestedloop, sieve), so heavy dataflow-transform passes would inflate a micro-benchmark's runtime unacceptably; accordingly RuntimeCost weights are kept low across the table so the selector avoids deploying BCF/FLA on the hot leaf loops while still permitting them where features indicate cold code. SUB gets the highest combined security/diversity weight because instruction substitution is nearly free at runtime and size yet meaningfully hardens a 634-byte binary where every instruction is analytically valuable. FLA carries the highest SecurityGain (flattening main's dispatch of the benchmark suite is the single biggest reversal deterrent) but moderate Runtime/SizeCost so it is applied selectively rather than globally. IBR is weighted strongly since indirect branches frustrate static control-flow recovery cheaply, and SPLIT is cheap coverage that enlarges basic-block inventory for the other passes. ICALL is moderate: there are few call sites (methcall-style dispatch) and indirecting them adds reversal friction at low risk. IGV is the weakest fit because this program has minimal global state, so its marginal gain is low; it remains enabled with modest weights for diversity rather than disabled.
